A B S T R A C T
This work investigated the influence of Sodium 3- (benzothiazole-2 -ylthio)- 1- propanesulfonate (ZPS) as a single
additive on performance of copper foil. Electrochemical analysis indicates that ZPS is of accelerating effect
during electroplating. Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM confirm that Copper growth obeys 3D diffusion-
controlled instantaneous nucleation and growth process, with ZPS significantly increasing the density of
active sites. A comprehensive theoretical framework combining density functional theory calculations, molecula
dynamics simulations, and in situ infrared spectroscopy elucidates an adsorption-capturing acceleration mech-
anism: ZPS can adsorb on copper surface and “catch” free Cu<sup>2+</sup> to the active sites to accelerate the electro-
chemical reduction process coupled with adsorbed Cl<sup>−</sup> . Furthermore, a Turing oscillation growth model,
supported by finite element simulations and AFM analysis, is proposed to describe the morphological evolution,
wherein ZPS preferentially accumulates at valley regions, improving surface flatness through cyclic peak-valley
transfer, though with inherently limited ultimate smoothing. Structurally, XRD shows ZPS promotes Cu (220)
orientation, while HRTEM confirms the presence of twin boundaries, and lattice fringe measurements reveal a
transition from (111)-dominated to (220)-dominated regions upon ZPS addition. Electron backscatter diffraction
(EBSD) further indicates grain refinement (mean size from 3.29 μm to 2.60 μm) and increased twin-boundary
density, which contribute to strengthening via Hall-Petch and dislocation-blocking effects. In terms of perfor-
mance, ZPS improves surface morphology and reduces roughness. Mechanical properties are optimized at
30 mg/L ZPS, with tensile strength reaching 331 MPa and elongation 3.78 %. Finite-element simulation of high
frequency signal transmission demonstrates that the lowered roughness effectively mitigates the skin effect,
reducing signal loss. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive mechanistic understanding of ZPS and dem
onstrates its potential as a single additive for producing high-performance electrolytic copper foils.

In this work, a novel accelerating additive, namely, accelerator
(benzothiazole-2 -ylthio)- 1- propanesulfonate (ZPS) is introduced to
prepare copper foil. Electrochemical analysis method, including cyclic
voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectra, was used to study the
effect of ZPS in cathode surface. Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM
was used to investigate the nucleation and growth process. DFT calcu
lation, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and in situ infrared spec-
troscopy is used to study the accelerating mechanism on the cathode
surface. Besides, growth model of copper foil under the influence of ZPS
was established based on finite element (FE) simulation. The phase
structure and surface morphology under the influence of ZPS is also
investigated, while tensile strength and elongation of copper foil is
evaluated. Based on FE simulation, the skin effect is studied for copper
foil with different surface roughness.

3. Results and discussion
3.1. Electrochemical and nucleation study
In this part, the influence of ZPS on cathode process was investigated.
The influencing effect of ZPS on copper electrodeposition was studied by
applying cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance
spectra (EIS), while the nucleation and growth of copper foil was studied
by chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM.
Fig. 1a1 shows the effects of ZPS on electrochemical reduction of
\mathrm { { C u ^ { 2 + } } }
and the onset potential was about −0.525 V. After the introduction
of ZPS, the onset potential shifted positively. When ZPS concentration
was 40 mg/L, the onset potential was increased to about −0.425 V,
indicating that ZPS is of depolarization effect during copper electrode-
position. Besides, it is obvious that the anodic stripping area saw an
increase with the rising of ZPS concentration, which demonstrates that
the number of deposited copper during cathodic reactions was increased
with the addition of ZPS, resulting in the increase of anodic stripping
area. As a result, the anodic stripping coulomb was calculated to
quantitively evaluate the accelerating effect [29], as shown in fig 1a2.

\mathrm { C } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }

4. Conclusion
In this study, additive Sodium 3-(benzothiazole-2-ylthio)-1-pro
panesulfonate (ZPS) has been systematically investigated for copper foil
electrodeposition. Cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance
spectra indicate that ZPS is of accelerating effect during electroplating.
Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM shows that the 3D diffusion
controlled instantaneous nucleation and growth model is not changed
but the active sites are increased by ZPS. Theoretical analysis suggests
that ZPS can adsorb on copper surface and catch free
\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + }
by -SO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> to
accelerate the electro-reduction coupled with adsorbed Cl<sup>−</sup> through
“bridging effect”. Adsorption-capturing accelerating mechanism was
proposed. Molecular dynamics simulation and in situ infrared spectros-
copy verify the improved adsorption property of ZPS with increased
cathodic polarization. A Turing oscillation growth model, validated by
finite-element simulation and AFM, reveals that ZPS accumulates in
valleys to locally accelerate growth, improving flatness via cyclic peak-
valley transfer, but the smoothing effect is ultimately constrained by this
oscillation. Structural characterization demonstrates that ZPS selec-
tively promotes the Cu (220) crystal orientation and suppresses the
(200) plane, while HRTEM directly visualizes twin boundaries, with
lattice fringes showing a shift from (111) to (220) in twin-vicinity re-
gions upon ZPS addition. EBSD confirms grain refinement (mean grain
size reduced from 3.29 μm to 2.60 μm) and a marked increase in twin-
boundary density, which together enhance mechanical performance
through Hall-Petch strengthening and dislocation obstruction.
Regarding copper foil performance, surface morphology is noticeably
improved, while the optimal mechanical properties are achieved at
30 mg/L ZPS, yielding a tensile strength of 331 MPa and elongation of
3.78 %, attributed to grain refinement and twin-boundary
strengthening. Finite-element simulation of skin effect demonstrates
that the reduced roughness significantly lowers signal loss. Collectively,
this work not only establishes ZPS as an effective single additive for
industrial copper foil production but also advances the fundamental
understanding of additive-induced structure-property relationships, of-
fering a solid foundation for future additive design and process
optimization.
